name: History trivia (easy)
description: 50 easy questions about world and US history, from ancient times to about 2000. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: For which ancient Egyptian pharaoh was the Great Pyramid of Giza built as a tomb?
items.explain: The Great Pyramid was built for Khufu, the second king of Egypt's 4th dynasty, around 4,500 years ago.

items.question: What was the main purpose of the Great Pyramid of Giza?
answers: A royal tomb for a pharaoh
items.correct: A royal tomb for a pharaoh
items.explain: The Great Pyramid was constructed as a royal tomb for Pharaoh Khufu.

items.question: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is the only one still standing today?
items.explain: Khufu's Great Pyramid at Giza is the only one of the ancient wonders that survives.

source.title: Great Pyramid of Giza - World History Encyclopedia

items.question: What did the Romans call March 15, the day on which Julius Caesar was assassinated in 44 BC?
items.explain: Caesar was killed on the Ides of March, which fell on March 15.

items.question: Which Roman senator, together with Gaius Cassius Longinus, led the plot to kill Julius Caesar?
items.explain: The conspiracy of roughly 60 men was led by Cassius and Marcus Junius Brutus.

items.question: Who emerged from the civil wars after Caesar's death to become Rome's first emperor?
items.explain: Caesar's grand-nephew Octavian won the civil wars and became Augustus, the first Roman emperor.

items.question: In early 44 BC, which title gave Julius Caesar rule over Rome with no time limit?
items.explain: Caesar was named dictator perpetuo, meaning dictator in perpetuity, in early 44 BC.

items.question: In which year did King John of England seal the Magna Carta?
items.explain: King John set his seal to Magna Carta on 15 June 1215.

items.question: At which meadow beside the River Thames did King John seal the Magna Carta?
items.explain: The charter was drafted at Runnymede, a meadow by the Thames, and sealed there in 1215.

items.question: What does the Latin name "Magna Carta" mean in English?
items.explain: Magna Carta translates as "Great Charter".

items.question: Columbus's 1492 voyage across the Atlantic was financed by the rulers of which country?
items.explain: Columbus won the sponsorship of Spain's monarchs, Ferdinand II and Isabella I.

source.title: Early career and voyages of Christopher Columbus

items.question: Which of these was one of the three ships Columbus sailed on his first voyage in 1492?
items.explain: Columbus set out with the Santa María, the Niña and the Pinta.

source.title: Early career and voyages of Christopher Columbus

items.question: Columbus sailed west in 1492 hoping to reach which continent?
items.explain: Columbus hoped to reach Asia by sailing west across what he thought was open sea.

source.title: Early career and voyages of Christopher Columbus

items.question: Columbus's first landfall in the Americas, in October 1492, was in what is now which island country?
items.explain: Land was sighted in the Bahamas on October 12, 1492, before he explored Cuba and Hispaniola.

source.title: Early career and voyages of Christopher Columbus

items.question: Who was the principal author of the US Declaration of Independence?
items.explain: The drafting committee gave the actual writing of the Declaration to Thomas Jefferson.

items.question: On what date did the Continental Congress approve the Declaration of Independence?
items.explain: The Continental Congress approved the Declaration on July 4, 1776, the date celebrated as American independence.

items.question: The Declaration of Independence announced the separation of 13 North American colonies from which country?
items.explain: With the Declaration, the 13 American colonies severed their political ties to Great Britain.

source.title: Milestones in the History of U.S. Foreign Relations - Office of the Historian

items.question: Which US president issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863?
items.explain: Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation during the third year of the Civil War.

items.question: Juneteenth marks the arrival of the promise of freedom to about 250,000 enslaved people in which state?
items.explain: Freedom reached the enslaved people of Texas two and a half years after Lincoln's proclamation, once Union victory was secured.

source.title: National Archives To Display Emancipation Proclamation and 'Juneteenth' General Order No. 3

items.question: Whom did Lincoln's 1863 Emancipation Proclamation declare free?
answers: Every enslaved person in the whole United States
Only enslaved people held in the loyal border states
Enslaved people held in areas still in revolt
Only enslaved people who had joined the Union army
items.correct: Enslaved people held in areas still in revolt
items.explain: The proclamation freed slaves in areas still in rebellion, and it left slavery in the loyal border states untouched.

source.title: The Original Emancipation Proclamation on Display at the National Archives and Records Administration

items.question: What was the Bastille, the Paris building stormed on July 14, 1789?
answers: A royal palace and hunting lodge
A medieval fortress and political prison
items.correct: A medieval fortress and political prison
items.explain: The Bastille was a medieval fortress, armory and political prison that became a symbol of royal tyranny.

items.question: Which French king was on the throne when the Bastille was stormed in 1789?
items.explain: Louis XVI was king in July 1789, when his dismissal of his finance minister Necker helped set off the crisis in Paris.

items.question: The storming of the Bastille in July 1789 was the flashpoint of which revolution?
items.explain: The storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789 was a pivotal event in the French Revolution.

items.question: Which French emperor suffered his final defeat at the Battle of Waterloo?
items.explain: Waterloo was Napoleon's final defeat, ending 23 years of recurrent warfare between France and the other powers of Europe.

items.question: Which British commander led the allied army that defeated Napoleon at Waterloo?
items.explain: Napoleon was beaten by the Duke of Wellington's combined allied army and a Prussian army under Blücher.

items.question: The Battle of Waterloo was fought near a village in what is now which country?
items.explain: The battle was fought south of Brussels near the village of Waterloo, in present-day Belgium.

items.question: In which year was the Battle of Waterloo fought?
items.explain: The battle took place on 18 June 1815.

items.question: The 1914 assassination of which archduke was the immediate cause of World War I?
items.explain: The killing of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, on June 28, 1914 sparked the war.

items.question: After the 1914 assassination of the Austro-Hungarian heir, which country did Austria-Hungary declare war on?
items.explain: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July 1914, and the conflict spread as other powers took sides.

source.title: Outbreak of the First World War

items.question: In which city was the Austro-Hungarian heir shot on June 28, 1914, sparking World War I?
items.explain: The assassination happened in Sarajevo, in Bosnia, and was the catalyst for World War I.

items.question: Which US president addressed Congress after Pearl Harbor, calling December 7, 1941 "a date which will live in infamy"?
items.explain: President Franklin D. Roosevelt gave the speech the day after the attack and asked Congress to recognize a state of war with Japan.

source.title: Pearl Harbor: December 7 Attack, Deaths & Summary

items.question: Which country launched the surprise attack on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941?
items.explain: Japan carried out the surprise aerial attack on the US naval base on Oahu, Hawaii.

items.question: The 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor drew the United States into which conflict?
items.explain: The attack precipitated the entry of the United States into World War II.

items.question: On what date did the Allied D-Day landings in Normandy take place?
items.explain: The Normandy invasion, known as D-Day, was launched on June 6, 1944.

items.question: What was the code name for the Allied invasion of Normandy in 1944?
items.explain: Operation Overlord was the code name for the Normandy invasion that began on D-Day.

source.title: D-Day: Learn about the D-Day Invasion

items.question: Which US general led the Allied force that landed in Normandy on D-Day?
items.explain: An Allied force led by Gen. Dwight D. Eisenhower launched the invasion on June 6, 1944.

items.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
items.explain: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989.

items.question: In which year were East and West Germany formally reunited?
items.explain: Germany reunited on 3 October 1990, about 11 months after the Berlin Wall fell.

source.title: What Was The Berlin Wall And How Did It Fall? - The Cold War

items.question: The fall of the Berlin Wall is seen as the symbolic end of which long standoff?
items.explain: The wall's fall symbolized the end of the Cold War division between East and West.

items.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon, during the Apollo 11 mission?
items.explain: Neil Armstrong, commander of Apollo 11, was the first human to walk on the surface of the Moon.

items.question: Which Apollo 11 astronaut stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module while two crewmates landed on the Moon?
items.explain: Armstrong and Aldrin took the lunar module down to the surface, while Michael Collins remained in the command module.

source.title: 1969 Apollo 11 Moon Landing: Timeline, Facts, Video

items.question: In which year did Apollo 11 land the first humans on the Moon?
items.explain: Apollo 11 launched on July 16, 1969, and Armstrong stepped onto the Moon that July.

items.question: What was the name of the Apollo 11 lunar module that landed on the Moon?
items.explain: Armstrong and Aldrin landed in the lunar module Eagle, while Collins flew the command module Columbia.

items.question: In April 1912, the Titanic sank after striking what?
items.explain: The British liner sank on its maiden voyage after hitting an iceberg in the North Atlantic.

items.question: On its maiden voyage from Southampton, England, the Titanic was bound for which city?
items.explain: The Titanic was heading from Southampton to New York City when it sank.

items.question: Approximately how many people died when the Titanic sank?
items.explain: Roughly 1,500 passengers and crew died in the sinking.

source.title: The Titanic: Deaths, Dates, Sinking & Facts

items.question: In which century did the Black Death devastate Europe?
items.explain: The Black Death ravaged Europe between 1347 and 1351, in the 14th century.

items.question: The Black Death reached Europe aboard ships carrying fleas that lived on which animals?
items.explain: The plague probably reached Sicily in 1347 on Genoese ships carrying flea-laden rats.

source.title: History of the Plague: An Ancient Pandemic for the Age of COVID-19 - PMC

items.question: Why was the 14th-century plague nicknamed the "Black Death"?
answers: Black spots appeared on the skin of many victims
Mourners across Europe wore black for years
Victims' bodies were burned and turned to ash
It spread mostly during moonless winter nights
items.correct: Black spots appeared on the skin of many victims
items.explain: The usual explanation is the black spots that developed on the skin of many victims. Some historians think the name came later, from a Latin phrase meaning "dreadful death".

items.question: On which continent did the plague that caused the Black Death originate?
items.explain: The plague originated in Asia and spread westward along trade routes to reach Europe.
